clue.text: Couple gave money to Republican instead of Democrat

indicators.note: says one letter takes the place of another in the word

parts.note: to have paid is to have given money

explanation.surface: A donor switches their political contribution from one American party to the other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to Republican instead of Democrat' tells you to swap the D of PAID for R.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a pair is two things or people taken together.

clue.text: Maybe Bach read French at the Royal Academy of Arts? Not initially

parts.note: lu is the French past participle of lire, to read
taken as written
RA stands for the Royal Academy (of Arts) in London

indicators.note: picks out only the opening letter of the word Not

explanation.surface: A question whether the composer studied French at a London art institution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not initially' reads as qualifying the question but simply supplies N.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: J S Bach belonged to the Protestant church founded on Martin Luther's teaching, hence 'Maybe'.

clue.text: Art museum delaying its opening provokes an abnormal reaction

indicators.note: the first letter of the museum word is held back until later in the word

parts.note: a gallery is a museum where art is shown

explanation.surface: A gallery's late opening causes outrage among visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letter G moves from the front of GALLERY to sit just before the final Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical sense: an allergy is the body's overreaction to something harmless like pollen.

clue.text: Lucky escapes from tight-fisted young women

parts.note: near is an old word for stingy or mean
misses are girls or young unmarried women

explanation.surface: Some narrow escapes from stingy girls.
explanation.walkthrough: NEAR meaning mean with money is a British usage the solver may not expect.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a close call where disaster was only just avoided is a lucky escape.

clue.text: Reserved return call curbed by result of Ripper's action?

indicators.note: the call word is held inside the tear word

parts.note: a rent is a tear, what ripping leaves behind

indicators.note: the word for call is read backwards

parts.note: to cite is to summon or call, as to court

explanation.surface: A reserved person's reply is muted by the shock of a Jack the Ripper killing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ripper' suggests the Victorian murderer, but it means anyone who rips, and 'return' turns the call word round before it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone reticent is reserved and slow to reveal their thoughts.

clue.text: A clergyman returns to Norfolk town briefly to see singing dame

indicators.note: the clergyman with A in front is read backwards

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a member of the clergy

indicators.note: the town's name is cut short, keeping only its second word

parts.note: King's Lynn is a market town in Norfolk, an English county

explanation.surface: A vicar goes back to King's Lynn to watch a famous singer perform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns A REV into VERA; KING'S LYNN, a town in the English county of Norfolk, shortened gives LYNN.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Vera Lynn was the British wartime 'Forces' Sweetheart' singer, made a Dame in 1975.

clue.text: Backing group of Suzanne Vega quits

indicators.note: the run of letters is read from right to left
a cluster of letters is taken from inside the singer's name

explanation.surface: The backing band of the singer Suzanne Vega resigns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing group' looks like a band but splits into two signals: NEVE is in suzanNE VEga, and 'Backing' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: being quits with someone means owing nothing either way, all square.

clue.text: Landlord engrossed by Dune novel is not familiar with classical works?

indicators.note: the landlord word sits inside the rearranged letters
new or fresh, so the letters of Dune are made anew

parts.note: a landlord lets property, so is a letter

explanation.surface: A landlord absorbed in Frank Herbert's Dune has never read the classics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like it describes Dune but signals the anagram of DUNE to UNED, which holds LETTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: unlettered means unlearned, without the literary education that classical reading once marked.

clue.text: Athenian drama has American university in a spin

indicators.note: the combined letters are turned round

parts.note: No (or Noh) is classical Japanese drama
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: A Greek play leaves a US college in turmoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Athenian drama' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just 'Athenian'; 'drama' gives NO.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Shakespeare's Timon of Athens is about a citizen of ancient Athens.

clue.text: A Roman Catholic monarch is hiding in diocese? I have no 14

indicators.note: the pieces are tucked away inside the diocese word

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese
HM stands for His or Her Majesty

explanation.surface: A Catholic king concealed in a bishop's territory has no clue what is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is IDEA, so the definition reads 'I have no idea'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the colloquial reply admitting you do not know, inviting the asker to look for themselves.

clue.text: Hairpiece exhibited by maiden in front of Queen and King? Not quite

indicators.note: places the maiden letter ahead of the rest

parts.note: M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for king is cut off

explanation.surface: A wig on show, worn by a girl standing before the royal couple, almost.
explanation.walkthrough: A merkin is specifically a pubic wig, which gives 'Hairpiece' its cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal sense: a merkin is an artificial hair covering, a wig for the pubic area.

clue.text: Doctor Strangelove with split character waiting with Vladimir on the stage

definitions.text: character waiting with Vladimir on the stage

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged
the title is divided, its love half replaced by the zero letter O, as love is nil in tennis

parts.note: the film title, which splits into strange and love

explanation.surface: The film's Dr Strangelove has a split personality, waiting alongside Vladimir in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr Strangelove is split into STRANGE + LOVE; love is O (nil in tennis), and 'Doctor' rearranges STRANGEO.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: in Beckett's play Waiting for Godot, two tramps, Vladimir and his companion, wait onstage.

clue.text: Sheepish fake journalist's drinking mug

parts.note: a sham is a fake

indicators.note: the journalist takes in the face word as if swallowing it

parts.note: ED, an editor, with 's read as 'is'
mug is slang for face

explanation.surface: A phoney reporter, embarrassed, sipping from a mug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mug' looks like a cup to drink from, but is slang for FACE, which ED surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: shamefaced means embarrassed or guilty-looking, as sheepish does.

clue.text: Every so often kiddies will get a brainwave?

indicators.note: only some letters at regular gaps in kiddies are kept

explanation.surface: Every now and then children come up with a bright notion.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of kiddies gives IDE, then A is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a brainwave is a sudden bright thought, a notion.

clue.text: Instrument for collecting water in the country

indicators.note: the instrument word gathers the water word inside it

parts.note: uke is short for ukulele
rain is water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: Some device used for gathering water out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the country' looks like rural land as opposed to town, but names a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Ukraine is a nation in eastern Europe.

clue.text: Greek NGO failed to support family movie

indicators.note: in a down answer this part sits below the family word, holding it up

parts.note: kin are one's relatives

indicators.note: the letters break down into a new order

explanation.surface: A Greek charity collapses while trying to help a family-friendly film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'family movie' suggests a film for all ages; 'family' is KIN. 'failed' scrambles GK with NGO into GKONG.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the 1933 film about a giant ape climbing the Empire State Building.

clue.text: Follow instructions when tackling model's weight problem

indicators.note: the obeying word grips the model word inside it

parts.note: to obey is to do what one is told
to model for an artist is to sit; the 's is just possessive surface

explanation.surface: Following a diet plan to tackle a model's weight issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' means pose for a painter, SIT, not a fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: obesity is the medical condition of being dangerously overweight.

clue.text: Amusing repartee is second-rate these days and in decline

parts.note: B grade is second class
AD, anno Domini, the present era
to age is to grow old and decline

explanation.surface: Witty banter has become mediocre nowadays and is falling off.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening reads as a complaint about modern wit, but it breaks into four small pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: badinage is light, playful teasing conversation.

clue.text: Oily crooked politician entering a state capital

indicators.note: the politician goes into the rearranged letters
bent out of shape, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A slimy corrupt politician arrives in a state capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' rearranges the letters of Oily to OLYI, with the politician entering before the final I.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Olympia is the capital city of Washington State in the USA.

clue.text: Former resident in prison cell

indicators.note: resident in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A one-time inmate of a jail cell.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: once as an adjective means former, as in 'the once king'.

clue.text: German louts merrily downing Double Diamonds? This is very rare

indicators.note: the jumbled louts swallow the diamonds pair
in a drunken, jolly way, so the letters are jumbled
says the diamonds letter is written twice over

parts.note: D abbreviates diamonds, the card suit

explanation.surface: Tipsy German yobs knocking back pints of Double Diamond beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Double Diamond was a well-known British bitter, so 'downing' suggests drinking; 'merrily' rearranges louts to OLUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something described as gold dust is scarce and highly prized.

clue.text: Starting late, China's ready to cut energy waste

indicators.note: the trimmed currency goes into the energy word

parts.note: go means vigour or energy

indicators.note: the first letter is dropped, so the word begins later

parts.note: the yuan is China's currency; ready is slang for cash

explanation.surface: Delayed, China is prepared to reduce wasted energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is British slang for money, so 'China's ready' is YUAN; 'Starting late' loses its Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: guano is seabird or bat droppings, a kind of waste used as fertiliser.

clue.text: Anger, say, about Kubrick's last film

indicators.note: the sin word goes around the letter

parts.note: anger is one of the seven deadly sins

indicators.note: only the final letter of Kubrick's is used

explanation.surface: Fury, perhaps, over Stanley Kubrick's final movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' looks like a movie but means a thin layer, as skin on custard.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a film is a thin covering layer, like the skin on hot milk.

clue.text: Woman from 15 gives thumbs up to Nazi terrorist militia backed by North America

indicators.note: the militia letters have the next piece placed behind them

parts.note: a thumbs-up signals OK
the SA, Sturmabteilung, were the Nazi brownshirts

explanation.surface: A Ukrainian woman approves of a fascist paramilitary group funded from America.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 is UKRAINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Oksana is a common girl's name in Ukraine.

clue.text: Turgidson finally slices bananas with tool for scraping plant

indicators.note: that letter cuts into the crazy word

parts.note: bananas is slang for mad

indicators.note: only the closing letter of Turgidson is kept

parts.note: a rake scrapes leaves and soil together

explanation.surface: General Turgidson of Dr Strangelove goes crazy, attacking with a garden tool.
explanation.walkthrough: Turgidson and Group Captain Mandrake are both characters in Dr Strangelove, so the answer is a sly theme link.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: mandrake is a Mediterranean herb with a forked root, steeped in folklore.

clue.text: Job Watch sees ten laid off

indicators.note: the ten letter is dismissed from the word

parts.note: Rolex is a famous make of watch
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Employment watchdog notes ten workers made redundant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid off' sounds like job losses but drops X from ROLEX.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a role is a function or position, a job.

clue.text: A French commander getting involved in wild binge is inappropriate

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: the officer letters go into the middle of the scrambled word
out of control, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Com is a standard abbreviation for Commander

explanation.surface: A French officer joining a drunken spree is behaving improperly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' reorders the spree word into BEING, which the officer's letters then enter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: unbecoming behaviour is unseemly or not fitting.

clue.text: See 6
